title: Material Conservation Studio
description: A luxury interior design studio where a SheenWoodLeatherSofa, a decorative Corset, and an Avocado sit on a pedestal. The user redistributes a fixed budget of material energy across the three objects, adjusting roughness, metalness, emissive intensity, and sheen, while a conservation law ensures the total material energy always sums to 1.0. Full undo/redo support tracks every adjustment.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Material Conservation Studio. Load three GLB assets: SheenWoodLeatherSofa.glb centered at origin on a ground plane, Corset.glb floating slightly above the left armrest, and Avocado.glb scaled up 15x on a small pedestal to the right of the sofa. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,5) with OrbitControls. Add an HDR-style lighting rig: one DirectionalLight, one HemisphereLight, and two colored PointLights for dramatic effect. Implement a material energy conservation system: define a total energy budget of 1.0 distributed across three objects. Each object has four material channels: roughness, metalness, emissiveIntensity, and sheen (or sheenRoughness). Create an HTML overlay panel with three collapsible sections (one per object), each containing four sliders for the channels. When any slider changes, compute that object's energy as the weighted sum of its four channels (weights: roughness=0.25, metalness=0.25, emissive=0.3, sheen=0.2). If the total across all three objects exceeds 1.0, proportionally scale down the OTHER two objects' channels to compensate, updating their sliders and materials in real-time. This is the conservation law and multi-input coupling. Clicking an object in the viewport with raycasting highlights it with an outline effect (set emissive color briefly) and expands its panel section. Implement an undo/redo stack (arrays of state snapshots) storing all 12 slider values. Add Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) buttons and keyboard shortcuts. Each slider change pushes a snapshot. Undo restores the previous snapshot and applies all material values. Redo moves forward. Display a real-time bar chart (three colored SVG bars in the overlay) showing each object's current energy share. The task requires at minimum 10 interactions: select object, adjust 4 channels across objects, trigger conservation rebalancing, undo twice, redo once, and reselect. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial properties where possible for sheen support on the sofa.
